On the 21st of September, the Prosecutor filed a motion for judicial notice of facts regarding Vukovar as mentioned in the Mrksic et al judgement. The question was put to you, and you answered then. However, it appears that when comparing the English transcript and the French transcript, there is some ambiguity regarding your position. Therefore, I shall put the question to you again. Are you going to file a written response or not?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have already made myself clear, orally. I said that if that motion had been properly filed, I would have made a written response, item by item, concerning the facts in question. But since these facts were established in a non-final decision, then it's out of place for the Prosecution to make this motion. If it were a final judgement, then I would have found it purposeful to make a written response and answer point by point. As it is, I reject it because the Prosecution is making this motion based on the trial judgement, which is not final.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second question. I'm now turning to the Prosecution, Ms. Biersay or Mr. Mundis. Regarding Vukovar, does the Prosecution maintain its motion, knowing that from the perspective of the Trial Chamber, we believe that we have a lot of witnesses who came to testify about Vukovar, and we wonder whether the motion is still necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Absolutely the motion is still necessary, and the Prosecution stands by the motion. To briefly respond to what the accused has said, of course, the jurisprudence of the Tribunal is such that one Trial Chamber may take judicial notice of adjudicated facts from the Trial Chamber's finding in another case with respect to those matters which are not the subject of an appeal from the first Trial Chamber's decision. The material that we've put before Your Honours in our motion of 25 September 2008 was limited to those issues which were not under appeal and which could, therefore, be considered to be final; and therefore would be ripe for consideration by this Trial Chamber. And so we do stand by our motion, and we do --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber will look into each and every fact.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Mr. Mundis were right, well, then the Prosecution should first provide me with all the appeals to the judgement so that I can convince myself that this wasn't appealed. But this is just hot air. There's no evidence. There are two brief administrative matters I'd like to deal with, but it would be for open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Yes, you will have your question in time for that, but let's move straight away into private session, because what I have to say is important, and I need time to announce that because we have to stop at 1.15 because we're going to have the swearing in of a new Judge just after that. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, first of all, I'd like to inform you that I was provided with a request from the Prosecution according to which VS-1000 should be heard according to Rule 92 ter. You've already rejected the request and decided that the witness should appear viva voce. I've already presented arguments with regard to this matter, and I don't want this witness to testify pursuant to 92 ter. This witness is VS-1000. On the 27th of October - this is the second matter - I received information from the Prosecution concerning VS-18, dated the 19th of October. A few days ago, I received a note from the Prosecution in which they said they were withdrawing this submission. And then on two occasions, detention guards came and asked me to submit this to them. First of all, I couldn't find it. I thought it was an unimportant decision, and I had mislaid it. Then a representative of the Registry, yesterday or the day before, asked me for this document. I found the document last night, and today I'm asking Mr. Mundis whether he asked for this document to be returned to him. I asked him about that. He didn't know what I was asking about. And then I was told by a representative from the Registry that the Registry, in fact, wanted me to return this document. It's unheard of. How is it that the Registry has the right to ask for me to return a document to them, a document that the Prosecution decided not to file a submission? I won't return this to the Registry. As soon as I return to my cell, I'll shred this. If the Registry is defiant on this, they'll have to look through my cell. What has the Registrar got to do with this document? It's a public document, it has a confidential annex, so that I am very familiar with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the accused said he would conceal or hide the document in his cell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is all this about, Mr. Mundis, about VS-18? Apparently Mr. Seselj received a document and then you told him that you wanted to withdraw it? I don't understand the first thing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To be honest, Mr. President, I have no idea what Dr. Seselj is talking about. I have not filed any documents concerning VS-18. I have absolutely no idea what the accused is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Seselj, so we have no idea. Mr. Mundis is going to inquire about it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The representative of the Registry should inform you of this. Perhaps the representative of the Registry could say something. He is present. He asked me to return this document. It's a Prosecution document, and the Prosecution told me that this document was being withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, our legal officer is going to take over the Registrar's work. We're going to look into this. We're going to try and shed some light on this. You've got the document. Keep it, do whatever you want to do with it. I don't know anything about this document. It was just about time to adjourn. I wish you all a good weekend. We shall reconvene on Tuesday, Tuesday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of November, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.09 p.m.,
